items.stem: An element has 12\,\text{V} across it, with the reference **+** terminal at the top. A current of 10\,\text{mA} is measured **leaving** the **+** terminal. Find the power absorbed by the element, with sign.

misconceptionTraps.feedback: The magnitude is right but the sign is inverted. Power is absorbed ($P > 0$) only when current **enters** the **+** terminal; here it is leaving it.

steps: Under the passive sign convention, $P = VI$ is the power **absorbed** when current enters the **+** terminal.
Current **leaves** the **+** terminal, so the current is $-I$ relative to the convention and $P$ is negative.
A negative result means the element **delivers** 0.12 W to the rest of the circuit.
explanation.principle: The sign of absorbed power records the direction of energy flow; a magnitude without a sign is only half the answer.
hints: Which terminal does the current enter?
Absorbed power is positive only when current enters the + terminal.

misconceptionTraps.feedback: You subtracted the second source term. Both sources sit above ground and push current **into** node $A$, so both appear with the same sign on the right-hand side.

steps: Write KCL at node $A$, taking every branch current as leaving the node:
Collect the $V_A$ terms on the left and the source terms on the right:
$V_A\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} + \dfrac{1}{R_2} + \dfrac{1}{R_3}\right) = \dfrac{12}{R_1} + \dfrac{1.5}{R_3}$.
Sanity check: $V_A$ must fall between ground and the larger source, 12\,\text{V} — and it does.
explanation.principle: Nodal analysis is one KCL equation per unknown node; the coefficient of the node voltage is always the sum of the conductances touching it.
hints: Take every branch current as leaving the node, then set the sum to zero.
The self-conductance term is the sum of 1/R over all branches at the node.
